title: Rainforest insects
keyIdea: Insects are the animals there are most of in a rainforest: far more than jaguars, monkeys or birds. An insect has 6 legs, so a spider, with 8, is not one. Leaf-cutter ants cut leaves and carry them home, but they do not eat them: they chew the leaves to feed a fungus garden, and the ants eat the fungus. The blue morpho butterfly is bright blue on top of its wings and brown with eye spots underneath, so it flashes when it flies and hides when it shuts its wings. Rainforest insects come in many sizes, from a 1 cm ant to a Hercules beetle up to 17 cm long, and each kind has a job, such as carrying pollen or turning rotting wood into soil.
familyTip: On a walk or in the garden, count every animal you see for five minutes and keep two tallies: insects and everything else. Insects nearly always win. Look for ants carrying things home, and check the legs of a minibeast together: 6 legs means insect, 8 legs means spider.

visual.caption: Insect or not? Count the legs. Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: count the animals, farm with leaf-cutter ants, hide a blue morpho, measure insects, match insect jobs.

kid: A rainforest is full of animals. You might think of jaguars, monkeys and toucans. But most of the animals are tiny. They are insects! There are more insects in a rainforest than all the other animals put together. An insect has 6 legs. A spider has 8 legs, so it is not an insect.

Leaf-cutter ants are farmers. They cut bits of leaf and carry them home on their backs. But they do not eat the leaves! They chew them into mush. A fungus grows on the mush, like a soft white garden. The ants eat the fungus.

The blue morpho is a big butterfly. The tops of its wings are bright blue. Underneath they are brown, with spots that look like eyes. When it flies, the blue flashes. When it lands and shuts its wings, it looks like a dead leaf. Birds find it hard to see.

Some rainforest insects are tiny, like an ant. Some are huge. A Hercules beetle can be longer than your hand! Every insect has a job. Bees carry pollen from flower to flower. Beetle grubs eat old logs and help make new soil.
adult: Ages 5 to 7. This fits KS1 science: living things and their habitats, and naming common animals. It also links to hot places near the equator in KS1 geography. Insects are the most common animals in tropical rainforest. Terry Erwin sprayed the tops of 19 trees in Panama and found about 1,200 kinds of beetle (Erwin 1982). In Amazon forest, ants and termites make up about a third of the weight of all animals (Fittkau and Klinge 1973). Key words: insect, minibeast, 6 legs, leaf-cutter ant, fungus, colony, blue morpho, beetle, grub, pollen.

Leaf-cutter ants (Atta and Acromyrmex) cut pieces of leaf and carry them along clear trails to their nest. Underground, they chew the leaves into mulch. A fungus grows on the mulch, and the ants and their larvae eat the fungus. The ants cannot digest the leaves themselves. A big Atta nest can hold several million ants. These ants eat more plants than almost any other animal in the forests of Central and South America (Hölldobler and Wilson 2011; Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute).

Blue morphos have wings about 12 to 20 cm across. The blue comes from tiny scales that bounce light, not from a blue dye. Underneath, the wings are brown with eye spots. In flight the flashing blue is hard for a bird to follow. At rest, with wings shut, the butterfly looks like a dead leaf (Natural History Museum, London). The Hercules beetle of Central and South America can reach about 17 cm in males, horn included. Its grubs grow in rotting logs. Shiny green orchid bees carry pollen for orchids and Brazil nut trees.

Common mistakes: thinking the big, famous animals are the most common; thinking leaf-cutter ants eat the leaves they carry; thinking a blue morpho is blue on both sides; thinking all beetles are tiny; and calling a spider an insect. A spider is a minibeast, but it has 8 legs. In the lab your child counts 15 animals into two tallies, carries 3 leaves to an ant nest and feeds the ants, and keeps a morpho safe from a bird 3 times. Then they measure 4 insects against a 13 cm hand on a ruler, and match 3 insects to their jobs.

practice.prompt: Which animals are there most of in a rainforest?
practice.hint: Think about the two tallies in the lab. Which bar was longer?
practice.explain: Insects. There are more insects in a rainforest than all the other animals put together.

practice.prompt: You count {a} ants on a leaf and {b} beetles on a log. How many insects is that?
practice.hint: Start with the ants, then count on the beetles.
practice.explain: {a} ants and {b} beetles make {=a+b} insects. Ants and beetles both have 6 legs.

choices: A fungus they grow on the leaves
practice.hint: What grew in the nest after the ants carried the leaves home?
practice.explain: The ants chew the leaves to feed a fungus. Then the ants eat the fungus.

practice.prompt: {a} ants are carrying leaves home. {b} of them get home. How many are still on the trail?
practice.hint: Take the ants that got home away from all the ants.
practice.explain: {a} take away {b} leaves {=a-b} ants still on the trail.

practice.prompt: A spider has 8 legs. Is it an insect?
choices: Yes, it lives in the rainforest
practice.hint: Count the legs. How many legs does every insect have?
practice.explain: No. Every insect has 6 legs. A spider has 8 legs, so it is a minibeast but not an insect.

pool.prompt: Why do leaf-cutter ants carry leaves home?
pool.hint: The leaves are food, but not for the ants.
pool.explain: They chew the leaves into mush, and their fungus garden grows on it. The ants eat the fungus.

pool.prompt: A blue morpho lands and shuts its wings. What colour do you see?
pool.hint: Only one side of the wings is blue.
pool.explain: Brown with eye spots. The blue is only on top, so with shut wings the morpho looks like a dead leaf.

pool.prompt: How long can a Hercules beetle be?
pool.hint: Remember the ruler in the lab and the dashed line at the end of the hand.
pool.explain: A Hercules beetle can be about 17 cm long. That is longer than a child's hand.

pool.prompt: A leaf-cutter ant carries {a} pieces of leaf in the morning and {b} more after lunch. How many pieces is that?
pool.hint: Start at {a} and count on {b} more.
pool.explain: {a} pieces and {b} more make {=a+b} pieces of leaf for the fungus garden.

pool.prompt: Which insect carries pollen from flower to flower?
choices: A beetle grub in a log
pool.hint: Which one flies from flower to flower?
pool.explain: Orchid bees fly from flower to flower. Pollen sticks to them and helps new seeds grow.

pool.prompt: How many legs does every insect have?
pool.hint: A spider has 8 legs, and it is not an insect.
pool.explain: Every insect has 6 legs. Ants, beetles, bees and butterflies all have 6.

pool.prompt: A blue morpho is {a} cm wide. A leaf-cutter ant is 1 cm long. How many cm wider is the morpho?
pool.hint: Take the ant's length away from the morpho's width.
pool.explain: {a} take away 1 is {=a-1}. The morpho is {=a-1} cm wider than the ant is long.

pool.prompt: You see {a} insects and {b} other animals in the rainforest. How many more insects than other animals?
pool.hint: Take the other animals away from the insects.
pool.explain: {a} take away {b} is {=a-b}. There were {=a-b} more insects. Insects are the animals there are most of.

pool.prompt: What do Hercules beetle grubs do in the rainforest?
choices: Eat rotting wood and help make soil
Cut leaves for a fungus farm
pool.hint: The grubs live inside old fallen logs.
pool.explain: The grubs eat rotting wood in fallen logs. That helps turn old trees into soil.
